command:
set -eu
printf 'boot_id='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
printf 'os='; . /etc/os-release; printf '%s %s\n' "$ID" "$VERSION_ID"
printf 'pam_pwquality_rpm='; rpm -q libpwquality 2>/dev/null || true
printf '%s\n' '--- pwquality files ---'
ls -l /etc/security/pwquality.conf /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d 2>/dev/null || true
printf '%s\n' '--- effective non-comment config ---'
for f in /etc/security/pwquality.conf /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; printf '[%s]\n' "$f"; sed -n '/^[[:space:]]*#/d;/^[[:space:]]*$/d;p' "$f"; done
printf '%s\n' '--- PAM references ---'
grep -Rns 'pam_pwquality\|pam_passwdqc' /etc/pam.d/system-auth /etc/pam.d/password-auth 2>/dev/null || true
printf '%s\n' '--- service baseline ---'
systemctl is-system-running 2>/dev/null || true
systemctl is-active sshd 2>/dev/null || true
ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | grep ':22 ' || true

command:
set -eu
policy=/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/60-password-policy.conf
umask 022
printf '%s\n' '# Managed password complexity policy' 'minlen = 12' 'minclass = 3' > "$policy"
restorecon "$policy" 2>/dev/null || true
printf '%s\n' '--- installed policy ---'
stat -c '%A %U:%G %n' "$policy"
sed -n 'p' "$policy"

command:
set -u
check() {
  label=$1
  sample=$2
  out=$(printf '%s\n' "$sample" | pwscore 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  printf '%s rc=%s output=%s\n' "$label" "$rc" "$out"
}
check valid_12_chars_3_classes 'F7qL9vR2xB4m'
check invalid_11_chars_3_classes 'F7qL9vR2xB4'
check invalid_12_chars_2_classes 'f7ql9vr2xb4m'
printf '%s\n' '--- PAM enforcement paths ---'
grep -n 'pam_pwquality.so' /etc/pam.d/system-auth /etc/pam.d/password-auth
